gecko_provenance.method: GECKO-style enzyme-constrained pFBA (variant pool125ezk): scipy HiGHS LPs over [p, n, e] with S p - S n = 0, p_j + n_j <= sum_u 3600 kcat_u e_u on 2694 reactions, sum_u MW_u e_u <= 0.125 g/gDW (gecko3_yeast_default), kcat sigma_k 0.0; stage 1 max growth, stage 2 (growth held at 0.999999 of the stage-1 optimum, the usage columns scaled to capacity 3600 kcat_u e_u) min sum(p + n) with the usages free; NO measured proteome; gene deleted by fixing its units' usages at 0 and closing the reactions cobra.manipulation.knock_out_model_genes closes; written by ess_gecko_store.py

media_report.recipe: YPD-approx (YNB + 20 amino acids + uracil + adenine; peptone NOT modeled)
media_report.provenance: see the recipe's docstring in torchcell/metabolism/media.py

pool.name: gecko3_yeast_default
pool.quote: If the total cellular protein content $P _ { t o t }$ is $0 . 5 \mathrm { g } / \mathrm { g } \mathrm { D } \mathrm { C W } ,$ the metabolic enzyme fraction over all proteins f is 0.5 and the average saturation $\sigma$ factor is 0.5, then the 'ecModel.lb' entry for 'prot_pool_exchange' is $- 1 2 5 \mathrm { mg / gDCW } .$
pool.notes: L132 states the same product as a rule: 'the default maximum constraint without knowledge of any factors is $0 . 5 \times 0 . 5 \times 0 . 5 = 0 . 1 2 5 .$'. Both factors of 0.5 that are not P_tot are GECKO defaults rather than yeast measurements, so 0.125 is a sourced convention and not a measured pool.

gecko_provenance.mw_rule: MW_u [kDa = g/mmol] = sum over the unit's member genes of the SwissProt MW (yeast-GEM data/databases/swissprot.tsv joined on the systematic ORF name), one copy per subunit (the GEM records no subunit stoichiometry); defined only when every member gene has a SwissProt MW, nothing defaulted
gecko_provenance.kcat_rule: resolve_kcat_table, kcat_table ezkinetics: Database tiers skipped by the caller: predicted tier = median over ezkinetics (verified tables, admitted by own_class_band; restricted to ezkinetics against the EC-median lookup at 0.532) for every unit with a prediction, then the median of the 3709 database-tier values, 4.51 1/s (database tiers skipped: median of the predicted values). A complex takes the min over its subunits. A unit resolved to the organism default has NO kcat here; kcat_ceiling_sigma_k 0.0
gecko_provenance.program: variables [p, n, e] >= 0, v = p - n with the GEM box split exactly as parsimonious_reference_flux splits it; S p - S n = 0; for every reaction whose units all have a kcat and an MW, p_j + n_j - sum_{u: rho(u)=j} 3600 kcat_u e_u <= 0 (both directions draw on the same enzyme; isozymes add); sum_u MW_u e_u <= P_avail; stage 1 max (p_b - n_b) [minus lambda sum(p + n) for the lambda variants], stage 2 (if any) min sum(p + n) or min sum_u MW_u e_u subject to p_b - n_b >= 0.999999 z*; the usage columns enter the matrix as capacities e'_u = 3600 kcat_u e_u and are mapped back; an enzyme row binds when its stage-1 dual exceeds 1e-09 in magnitude; the pool dual is minus the stage-1 marginal of the pool row, in (1/h) per (g/gDW); a direction rule fixes lb >= 0 where delta_r G' <= -T and ub <= 0 where delta_r G' >= +T
gecko_provenance.pool_usage_rule: for stage-2 = flux: the minimum pool that carries the stage-2 flux (per enzyme-constrained reaction the surviving unit with the smallest MW_u / (3600 kcat_u) takes |v_j|), the stage-2 LP's own usage vector being degenerate; for stage-2 = enzyme_mass: the LP's own sum_u MW_u e_u; reported as a fraction of P_avail; nan where the variant has no pool. The allocation change per genotype is the number of units whose usage differs from the wild type's under the same rule and the mass moved, sum_u MW_u |e_u - e_u^wt|, as a fraction of P_avail
